repairs.resolution: Use codex_app_server only for the new operator route and version those inputs as operator-luna6-2; preserve historical routes and superseded v1 evidence.

outcomes: Blocked pools survive cross-run scheduling and worker composition recreation; known reset and unknown cooldown remain distinct.
Concurrent pollers admit one recovery probe; stale responses cannot erase newer exhaustion or shorten its block.
A skipped attempt spends no attempt or repair unit and occupies no capacity; missing stopped-launch proof prevents a replacement probe.
Only the exact frozen fallback is allowed. Retained +0 partial work is read and repaired to +1, adding the negative boundary assertion.
The same child, paths, budget, requested route and Astra primary survive fallback; two child attempts, one check, zero repair debits and zero outstanding reservations.
A recreated worker applies the retained handoff once; the primary accepts that source. Without an approved fallback the partial write remains deferred.
Authentication, unsupported route, throttling, outage and confirmed exhaustion have distinct classifications; unknown reset/allowance is not reported as available.
self_review: Selected primary checked failure causes, fixture isolation, unchanged historical defaults, explicit new scenario IDs, frozen route/authority/budget assertions and matching retained evidence.
limitations: Quota responses and counter launch proof are scripted; the Codex/Claude adapter cases supervise fake local peer processes.
No real subscription was exhausted and no paid API or billing setting was changed. Scripted counters do not measure live usage or remaining allowance.
Counter scenarios stop in IMPLEMENTING at child acceptance or quota deferral; they do not claim final candidate validation or human publication/merge approval.
No production runtime repair or full CI was needed.
